title: Trace continuity & adaptive tenant throttling for on‑prem collectors
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Customers running Dedicated and Private (VPC/on‑prem) deployments report intermittent loss of trace continuity during bursts and during collector failover. Lost trace links most commonly occur when tenant-scoped collectors evict buffered segments under backpressure or when sampled spans are dropped without preserving parent/trace identifiers. This causes debugging and SLO investigations for high-value enterprise customers to be noisy and slow.

Goal: Implement a small-surface change across the on‑prem collector and perimeter gateway that preserves trace continuity across retries and partial writes, plus an adaptive tenant throttling controller that keeps per-tenant ingest within defined SLOs while preserving a sample that accurately represents correlated latency/error signals.

Scope:
- Preserve trace-link metadata (trace_id, parent_id, sampling-bits) in the collector envelope and ensure it is retained even when spans are partially buffered or rewritten.
- Add a lightweight durable prefix cache for in-flight span fragments to stitch spans when backpressure causes reordered writes.
- Implement adaptive per-tenant sampling + soft-throttling (burst-aware) policy configurable via Console and exposed in the Private control plane.
- Provide dashboards and alerts showing trace-link loss rate, sampled-span representativeness, per-tenant ingest throttle events, and end-to-end latency regressions.

Out of scope: full redesign of collector storage, cluster sharding changes, or cross-tenant joins.
acceptance_criteria:
1) No increase in trace-link-loss rate in staging vs. baseline (<=0.2% additional loss during synthetic burst tests).
2) Adaptive throttling prevents per-tenant ingestion from exceeding configured soft-SLOs (example: 500 reqs/s) while maintaining sampled-span distribution within +/-10% of baseline on p50/p95 latency buckets.
3) End-to-end tests for collector failover show recovered trace stitching in <60s for reassembled fragments.
4) Config knobs exposed in Console with role-based access and audit log entries for changes.
5) Unit and e2e tests added; PR reviewed and merged; rollout doc and rollback steps published.
risks:
- Risk of increased per-span envelope size due to appended stitching metadata; mitigated via compact encoding and truncation policy.
- Incorrect sampling bias introduced by adaptive controller; mitigated by simulation on historical workloads and canarying.
- Backward compatibility with older Private control plane versions; mitigated by feature flag and opt-in rollout.
- Performance regression on low-latency paths; mitigate by microbenchmarks and kernel hotpath instrumentation.
alternatives:
1) Do nothing: continued debugging pain for customers (not acceptable).
2) Increase global sampling rate for on-prem tenants: simple but increases downstream cost and privacy surface.
3) Centralize all tenant buffering in a single service: heavy operational cost and increases blast radius.
Chosen: local conservative stitching + adaptive throttle to balance fidelity and cost.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flag behind "onprem.observability.stitching_v1" for Private control plane.
2) Stage in internal engineering clusters (staging-obs) with synthetic burst workload.
3) Canary to 2 small customers in Dedicated for 48h with increased tracing retention.
4) Monitor dashboards for 72h; if any regressions -> rollback flag.
5) Gradual expansion to remaining Dedicated customers over 2 weeks.
6) GA switch with docs and console UI enablement.
monitoring_dashboards:
- Trace Link Loss: ratio of spans with missing trace_id/parent_id (per-tenant, 1m and 5m).
- Sample Representativeness: distribution compare between full ingest (where available) and sampled spans (p50/p95/p99).
- Throttle Events: count of adaptive throttle activations and reasons (CPU/memory/ingest-rate).
- Stitching Latency: time between first fragment and final stitched span.
- Collector Health: queue depth, eviction rate, ephemeral cache hit/miss.
test_plan:
- Unit tests: envelope preservation, encoding/decoding, and prefixed-stitching algorithm.
- Integration: end-to-end from SDK->perimeter->collector->store with synthetic fragmentation.
- Load test: 100 tenants with burst profile (10k rps bursts) to validate throttling and memory bounds.
- Backward compat test: older control plane versions ignoring optional envelope fields.
- Security: ensure no tenant can read other tenant IDs or modify sampling policies.
comments: 2025-01-10 Maya Patel: Created ticket after postmortem with ACME Corp (customer) showed multiple lost traces during node drain. Link to postmortem: https://drive.google.com/document/d/pm-acme-trace-loss

2025-01-14 Liam O'Connor: Spike complete. Two approaches evaluated: (A) prefix durable cache in collector (low memory, fast lookup), (B) central sequencer rewrite (high cost). Chose (A). Spike repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs-spikes/pull/36

2025-01-20 Liam O'Connor: Microbenchmarks: stitching adds 0.7ms median overhead and 1.5% p99 on the critical path with compact encoding. Memory overhead bounded to per-tenant window. Added initial implementation in branch feat/stitching-v1.

2025-01-28 Maya Patel: Design review with Product and Security. Security asked for envelope HMAC for tamper-resistance (opt-in). Agreed to add config knob and default off for GA. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Trace+Stitching+Design
2025-01-30 Priya Singh (Infra): Integration note: collector sidecar requires a config map change to enable per-tenant quota hooks. Created infra ticket ENG-77250 to update Helm chart.

2025-02-02 Liam O'Connor: PR opened for collector and gateway changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/collector/pull/1245. Requesting review from @jamesw and @anne-cs. Running staging load test now; this ticket will block on infra chart update (ENG-77250).
